history.content: Why can't house prices be out of tune with salaries

House prices cannot be out of tune with salaries in the long term. The equilibrium median home price tends to align with the price supported by the median income.  House prices are only sustainable if people actually can afford to buy houses and if there's a massive disconnect between house prices and salaries, then house prices will fall eventually.  A hypothetical scenario where if house prices rise 1% faster than salaries indefinitely, the average house will become extremely expensive compared to the average salary in the far future, which is not plausible.
That means ppl in the NYC earn a lot!!!
The min wage in NYC was higher than the rest of NY state. However, cost of living differences are the big equalizer among states and area.

Is there federal help for the first time buyers?

Yes, there are federal programs available to assist first-time homebuyers in the United States. One such program is the Federal Housing Administration (FHA) first-time buyer program, which requires a 3.5% down payment. Another program is the Fannie Mae HomeReady program, which allows first-time buyers to purchase a foreclosed home from their inventory for as little as 3% down and possibly get up to 3% from the seller to apply toward closing costs. Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is required with this program. Additionally, there is the NACA program, which requires attending workshops and creating a detailed plan to prove readiness for homeownership.
